Hyperspectral data were acquired of the scene with a single line integration time of 200 ms. The line was swept over an 18-degree scene using a rotary stage adapter (Headwall Photonics, micro-hyperspec rotary stage) at a speed of 0.04 deg/sec for a total acquisition time of ~ 7.5 min. Final image dimensions were 1919 pixels x 2250 pixels x 376 wavelengths. Additional calibration data was collected for both hyperspectral imagers using a diffuse reflectance target with ~ 99% reflectance (Labsphere, USRT-99-100) in place of the algae in the scene with the exact acquisition parameters as the algae spectral data. Following the completion of data collection, three 200 uL samples were taken from each dish and placed in a 96-well plate along with three samples of media as a blank. The optical density (OD) was measured at 680 nm and 750 nm for each well using a microplate reader (Agilent BioTek Synergy NEO2). The average of the background-corrected triplicate measurements was calculated and used as a proxy for the algal concentration in each dish. 16 Figure 3: Photograph of lab experiment showing dishes with various P. celeri TG2 concentrations. OD readings are indicated on each dish. . Spectrally resolved reflectance spectra were processed by subtracting dark counts and converted to reflectance values by ratioing to the diffuse reflectance target (also with the dark counts subtracted). Hyperspectral image data (both snapshot and line-scan format) was converted to reflectance values on a per-pixel basis using the same method, performing a ratio to data collected from a diffuse reflectance target under the same conditions. Figure 4 shows representative spectra (top panel) and spectral images (bottom panel) from a P.celeri dilution experiment. The spectral shapes are similar from each measurement technology, but the spectral resolution is much lower with the snapshot imager and the spectral range reduced to 450-850 nm. The spectral data from the snapshot hyperspectral imager are also noisier, despite the averaging over 10 temporal snapshots and 703 spatial pixels. This is primarily due to the short integration time and the detector architecture; however, this noise could be potentially reduced by utilizing additional averaging over the time because the snapshot format provides rapid readout (up to 70 frames/sec). It is unlikely that the integration time can be increased much in this configuration because the dynamic range of the snapshot camera is already near full with the short integration time. The line-scan hyperspectral imager provides improved spectral and spatial resolution as compared to the snapshot imager, however while the individual acquisition time was short for each line, the configuration used in the experiment required a long scan time to scan the entire scene and each line was viewing many pixels outside the algal dishes.
